correctness.rationale: The skew Brownian transition density integrates to the explicit affine-in-bias survival probability. Conditional independence gives the exact annealed-minus-quenched variance identity. B_t is strictly decreasing so its variance is positive; derivatives of the survival probability at x=0 and x=L exclude zero gap for all finite t. Disjoint Gaussian boundary layers prove the short-time optimizer tends to 1. A uniform t^-1/2 Gaussian expansion identifies the variance polynomial (61 beta^2+2 beta+1)/180, giving the sharp t^-3 coefficient and interior long-time optimum -1/61. Continuity of the exact optimizer proves at least one crossing. Exact fractional and 55-digit numerical checks from extracted verify.py support the calculations, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The gap measures the component of outside-count fluctuations attributable to random initial positions, a natural physical quantity in finite-particle effusion. A tunable skew point is a concrete transport-control mechanism. The theorem establishes a nontrivial reversal of best junction bias over the physically distinguished short and long diffusion times, refines leading asymptotic equality to a sharp t^-3 law and supplies a 64-fold endpoint benchmark. It is a motivated full-parameter classification of optimum over an entire one-parameter family, not a routine isolated substitution.
